subject: [RFC PATCH] btrfs: trigger cow fixup via dirty_folio()

reviews.author: Qu Wenruo
reviews.summary: Reviewer Qu Wenruo suggested splitting the set/clear of the folio fixup flag into data and metadata specific functions to avoid exposing btrfs_is_subpage() checks, and proposed implementing btrfs_folio_set_fixup() and btrfs_folio_clear_fixup() helpers. They also recommended integrating fixup cancelling into the btrfs_folio_set_dirty() helper in a future cleanup/refactor series.
reviews.raw_body:
\u5728 2026/7/27 13:27, Boris Burkov \u5199\u9053:
[...]
>> Shouldn't we also check if we have cleared the last fixup bit and clear the
>> folio fixup flag?
>> [...]
>>> +void btrfs_folio_cancel_fixup(const struct btrfs_fs_info *fs_info,
>>> +			      struct folio *folio, u64 start, u32 len)
>>
>> Why not let IMPLEMNT_BTRFS_PAGE_OPS() to implement all the fixup helpers?
>>
> 
> I think the level 0 answer is it doesn't apply to metadata and the llm
> also went nuts messing with the macros when it tried to use them.

Right, metadata doesn't need such fixup handling at all, thus we will 
need to split the set/clear into (data|meta)_(set|clear)_func(), which 
is a little overkilled for a hot fix.

Although it would still be good to implement something like 
btrfs_folio_set_fixup() and btrfs_folio_clear_fixup(), so that we do not 
need to expose btrfs_is_subpage() checks.

And we can integrate the fixup cancelling into btrfs_folio_set_dirty() 
helper later, in a dedicated cleanup/refactor series.

Thanks,
Qu

2026-07-27.patch_summary: This patch proposes a new approach to trigger the COW (Copy-On-Write) fixup in Btrfs via the dirty_folio() function, which is used to handle folios that have been improperly dirtied during writeback. The current implementation uses an asynchronous worker to catch and fix such cases, but this patch aims to simplify the process by leveraging the dirty_folio() function. This change addresses a long-standing issue where a dio read may skip dirtying a folio if it is already clean by the end of the I/O operation, leading to potential data corruption. The patch maintains three critical invariants to ensure that each block is written exactly once: any dirty block is covered by delalloc or an ordered extent, any dirty block submitted into an OE will be written back within that OE, and any dirty block already submitted into an OE will not be resubmitted. This change aims to demonstrate a more complex solution to the problem and highlight the issues it must address.
